descriptionNullable:
# METAR Weather Observations — 26 Global Cities, 2024–2026

**958,338 raw METAR observations** (including SPECI special reports) from the primary airport weather stations of 26 major cities on 5 continents, covering **January 2024 through August 2026**.

## Why this dataset is different

Most weather datasets give you *daily summaries* or *hourly model reanalysis*. This one gives you the **actual raw METAR reports** issued by each station — the same observations used by aviation, and the ground truth behind most "official high temperature" records:

- **SPECI reports included** (372,730 of them, flagged with `is_speci=1`). Special reports are issued *between* routine hourly observations when conditions change rapidly. Daily-max temperatures computed from routine-only vs. SPECI-inclusive observations can differ by several degrees on 10–15% of days at some stations — if you've ever wondered why your computed daily max doesn't match a published record, this is usually why.
- **Full raw METAR text preserved** in every row. Temperature is pre-parsed for convenience, but wind, visibility, precipitation, cloud layers, pressure and remarks (including precise T-group temperatures to 0.1 °C) are all recoverable from the `metar` column with any METAR parser (e.g. the `metar` PyPI package).

## Files

### observations.csv (~100 MB)
| column | description |
|---|---|
| `station` | ICAO station identifier (e.g. KLGA, RJTT) |
| `valid_utc` | Observation timestamp, UTC, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` |
| `temp_c` | Air temperature in °C parsed from the report (0.1 °C resolution where the T-group is present) |
| `is_speci` | 1 = SPECI (special report), 0 = routine (hourly/half-hourly) observation |
| `metar` | Full raw METAR/SPECI text as issued |

### stations.csv
| column | description |
|---|---|
| `station` | ICAO identifier |
| `city` | City the station serves |
| `station_name` | Airport name |
| `country` | Country |

## Coverage

Toronto (CYYZ), Munich (EDDM), Helsinki (EFHK), London City (EGLC), Amsterdam (EHAM), Warsaw (EPWA), Atlanta (KATL), Austin (KAUS), Dallas (KDAL), Houston (KHOU), Los Angeles (KLAX), New York (KLGA), Miami (KMIA), Chicago (KORD), Seattle (KSEA), San Francisco (KSFO), Madrid (LEMD), Paris-Le Bourget (LFPB), Ankara (LTAC), Istanbul (LTFM), Tokyo Haneda (RJTT), Buenos Aires (SAEZ), Moscow Vnukovo (UUWW), Lucknow (VILK), Beijing (ZBAA), Shanghai Pudong (ZSPD).

24,840–53,862 observations per station (stations differ in routine cadence and SPECI frequency).

## Example uses

- Time-series forecasting of temperature at hourly/sub-hourly resolution
- Studying **daily maximum temperature** and how sampling frequency changes it (routine-only vs. SPECI-inclusive)
- Cross-city climate comparison over identical windows
- Parsing wind / visibility / weather phenomena from raw METAR text (NLP-ish structured extraction exercise)
- Benchmarking METAR parsers

## Provenance

Collected from the **Iowa Environmental Mesonet (IEM) ASOS/METAR archive** (`mesonet.agron.iastate.edu`), which archives observations distributed by NOAA and international METAR feeds. One request per station-year, routine and SPECI reports fetched explicitly, no interpolation — what the station issued is what's here.

Acknowledgment: thanks to the IEM for maintaining a free, well-run archive of global surface observations.

## Notes & caveats

- `temp_c` is as-parsed from the report; a handful of stations occasionally issue reports without a parseable temperature — those rows are absent.
- Timestamps are UTC; convert to local time before computing "daily" statistics for a city.
- 2026 coverage runs through August 1, 2026.
